10 Questions to Ask a Greige Fabric Manufacturer Before Placing a Bulk Order

Placing a bulk fabric order is a significant step.

Once production begins, changing a specification can become expensive, time-consuming or difficult.

That's why the best time to ask questions is before you place the order.

Whether you are an apparel manufacturer, textile business, exporter, fabric processor or sourcing professional, these 10 questions can help you have a more productive conversation with a greige fabric manufacturer.

1. What Is the Exact Fabric Construction?

Don't stop at “cotton fabric” or “lightweight fabric.” Ask for the actual construction, including relevant yarn count, EPI, PPI, weave and other specifications.

The more precisely the fabric is defined, the easier it is to reproduce the requirement.

2. Is the GSM Specified as Greige or Finished?

This is a small question that can prevent a major misunderstanding.

Greige and finished fabric can have different weights because processing changes the fabric.

Always establish which stage the stated GSM refers to.

3. What Is the Actual Usable Width?

Ask whether the stated width refers to:
● Total width
● Loom width
● Finished width
● Usable width The distinction can matter significantly for cutting and fabric consumption.

4. What Tolerances Apply?

No manufacturing process should be discussed only in terms of a single ideal number.

Ask what tolerance applies to:
● GSM
● Width
● Construction
● Quantity
● Other relevant parameters These should ideally be agreed before production.

5. Can You Provide an Approved Sample?

A physical reference is extremely valuable.

It gives the manufacturer a tangible standard to work toward and gives the buyer something against which bulk production can be evaluated.

6. How Is Bulk Production Checked?

Don't settle for “quality checked.” Ask what is checked, when it is checked and against what reference.

Depending on the product and agreement, quality checks can cover parameters such as weight, width, construction and appearance.

7. How Will Repeat Orders Be Matched?

If you expect to reorder the same fabric, ask how the manufacturer records the original requirement.

A repeat order should ideally refer back to an approved specification and sample rather than simply a product name or an old invoice.

8. What Is the Production Lead Time?

Ask for realistic production timelines and understand what starts the production clock.

This is particularly important when your own production schedule depends on the fabric arriving on time.

9. What Information Do You Need From Me?

This question is surprisingly useful.

A good manufacturer should be able to tell you exactly what they need: Fabric construction?

Quantity?

GSM?

Width?

Yarn count?

Composition?

Sample?

The clearer your initial enquiry, the easier it becomes to quote and manufacture correctly.

10. Can You Support My Requirement as It Grows?

Your first order may be small compared with your future requirement.

Ask whether the manufacturer's capabilities can support your expected growth and repeat requirements.

The Better Bulk-Order Checklist

Before confirming your order, make sure both sides are aligned on:
☑ Fabric construction
☑ Yarn count
☑ GSM
☑ EPI/PPI
☑ Width
☑ Composition
☑ Quantity
☑ Approved sample
☑ Tolerances
☑ Delivery expectations A clearly defined order reduces room for assumptions and in fabric sourcing, fewer assumptions usually mean fewer surprises.
